utterances.text: The answer is something of a problem caused by the accused not preparing his materials properly. We've been trying to track down private sessions or otherwise for witnesses. Perhaps this ought to be dealt with in private session itself, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, maybe these several assertions of Mr. Theunens could help confirm your assertions concerning the status of your volunteers, namely on page transcript 31489, Theunens refers to Mrksic's order - Mrksic was then the commander of the Guards Brigade - about the resubordination of the unit in Vukovar, and that applies to Seselj's volunteers too. On page 31524, Theunens says that one of the JNA commanders in his report said that he had problems with the engagement of certain units, meaning by that Seselj's volunteers and the Territorial Defence, and he says Seselj's volunteers participated in operations in Vukovar under JNA command. So he refers to this document. Then on page 31692, Theunens, their military expert, says that he had seen the war journal of the Guards Brigade referring to Seselj's volunteers. This is related in a way to what you said, namely that your volunteers were within the JNA.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Our volunteers were always part of the JNA. I keep repeating that most emphatically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Witness D1804, who testified on the 10th of February, 2004, page 31832, says that when the conflict began, volunteers such as Seselj's men, but he speaks in general about volunteers, participated in operations under JNA command. To the best of your knowledge, was that general practice, namely that volunteers could only go as part of the JNA, apart from those who wanted nothing to do with the JNA, such as the Serb Guard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... this business of reading out the transcript, going on and on and on. If you have a specific question, just raise it. And we don't want repetition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about Witness B. This was used by Mr. Nice to denote witnesses testifying about Bosnia. So this is not about Croatia. He says on page 31832: "When the conflicts broke out, volunteers such as Seselj's men participated in operations under the command of the JNA."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Seselj, was as follows: Was it so according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the armed conflict broke out in Bosnia, volunteers of the Serb Radical Party within JNA units participated in those conflicts. I mentioned the example of Zvornik. Before that, it was the Mostar theatre and several other locations. There is precise documentation about this in the General Staff of the JNA as to where they were sent and where they participated. It's no secret. I am proud of the participation of volunteers from the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, next question. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The next question concerns paragraph 34 of the Croatian indictment. We have not yet mentioned this paragraph, although it will seem very familiar to you because it's the same text running through all the paragraphs more or less. So look at paragraph 34 and tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says here -- let me just -- "From on or about the 1st of August, 1991, until June 1992 --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just ask the question. Just reflect the substance of it. There's no need to read out the content.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. It says here that I acted with participants known and unknown of the joint criminal enterprise and that I planned, instigated, ordered, committed, or otherwise aided and abetted and so on the planning, preparation, or execution of the persecutions of the Croat and other non-Serb civilian population. As you also are accused of this, tell me, did you in any way plan, instigate, order, commit, or otherwise aid and abet the persecution of Croat and other non-Serb civilians as mentioned in this paragraph, and according to what you know, did I in any way plan, instigate, order, and so on and so forth, what it says here in this paragraph 34?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither I nor you nor anyone else on the Serb side planned, instigated, ordered or aided and abetted or committed the persecution of the Croat and other non-Serb civilian population. This was not done systematically. It was not done in an organised manner. There were incidents where this was done, but all these incidents can be listed and the perpetrators can be identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you, with respect to anyone on the list of alleged participants in the so-called joint criminal enterprise, can you identify anyone in that list who may have planned, instigated, ordered, committed or otherwise aided and abetted this?

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that I have a negative opinion of many of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: VOJISLAV SESELJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: But as a serious witness I cannot say so-and-so did that but I did not see it. I was not an eyewitness. If any of them did anything like that, I attacked them publicly at the time, but I was not an eyewitness to what Aleksandar Vasiljevic was doing apart from what I learned for certain that he had done in Vukovar, Western Slavonia, and so on and so forth. I was not an eyewitness to what Arkan did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. You have answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if you're about to bring the hearing to a conclusion. If so, can I just confirm the position in respect of the matter raised in private session. It was as I -- perhaps we better deal with it in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, private session. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until tomorrow at 9.00 a.m.
